clues.text: Before a rioting crowd in Jerusalem, he took water and washed his hands, saying he was innocent of Jesus' blood.
While he sat on the judgment seat during Jesus' trial, his wife warned him about a troubling dream.
Inside the Praetorium, after Jesus spoke of testifying to the truth, this man asked, "What is truth?"
To satisfy the crowd at the feast, this governor released Barabbas and had Jesus flogged.
When the chief priests objected to the sign he had posted above Jesus on the cross, he refused to change it.
He and Herod had been enemies, but became friends the day Jesus was sent back and forth between them.
When Joseph of Arimathea asked for Jesus' body, he was surprised and asked a centurion if Jesus had already died.
